questions.question: Describe the general rule for the matchstick pattern 4, 7, 10, 13 in words and justify it from the picture.
questions.expected_answer: Multiply the number of squares by 3 and add 1. Each square owns 3 matches (top, bottom, right side) and one extra match closes the left side of the first square.

questions.question: Use the rule to find the number of matches for 100 squares and the number of squares for 151 matches.
Explain why no row of matchstick squares uses exactly 200 matches.
questions.expected_answer: 200 − 1 = 199, and 199 ÷ 3 is not a whole number (66 remainder 1), so 200 is not 3 × n + 1 for any whole n.
